name: 51 Pegasi
tagline: The first Sun-like star found to host an exoplanet — the discovery that opened a universe of worlds.
history: In October 1995 Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz announced a Jupiter-mass planet circling 51 Pegasi every 4.2 days — the first planet ever confirmed around a Sun-like star, and so close-in it defied every formation theory. 'Hot Jupiters' forced astronomy to rewrite how systems migrate and assemble; over 5,500 exoplanets later, the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics honored the discovery. The planet's IAU name, Dimidium, is Latin for 'half' — half the first step beyond our own system.
source: NASA Exoplanet Archive · Observatoire de Genève
